source_caption_text:
Footage of King Von and Chief Keef together in the studio back in 2019 resurfaces 👀

King Von and Chief Keef shared a relationship rooted in their common upbringing in Parkway Gardens, the South Side Chicago housing complex famously known as O’Block. Chief Keef broke out as a teenager in 2012, thrusting O’Block and the Chicago drill movement into the global music spotlight. During Keef’s meteoric rise, King Von was a prominent figure in the same neighborhood but was not yet making music, spending much of that era navigating legal troubles and extended periods of incarceration.

Although both men grew up in the same neighborhood and shared mutual acquaintances, they were never close personal friends or active musical collaborators. By the time King Von launched his own rap career in 2018 after signing with Lil Durk’s Only the Family (OTF) label, Chief Keef had long since relocated to Los Angeles and distanced himself from active involvement in Chicago block dynamics.

Despite the physical distance and occasional friction between their respective circles, King Von consistently expressed respect for Chief Keef in media interviews. Von publicly acknowledged Chief Keef as a trailblazer who paved the way for Chicago artists and permanently put their neighborhood on the map.
